summary: Renate Syed is an Indologist who earned her doctorate at the University of Munich (~1974–1982) under Dieter Schlingloff, Friedrich Wilhelm, and Gritli von Mitterwallner. She was attested as a Privatdozentin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.
Renjo Akamatsu (1841–1919) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied under Chō Sanshū and held a post at Ryukoku University.

Renshan Yang (1837–1911) was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the Jinling Scriptural Press (1897) and Jetavana Hermitage (1908). In 1910, he founded and headed the Buddhist Research Society. His students included Jian Ouyang, Tan Sitong, and Taixu.

René Gothóni (born 1950) is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1971–1977) and later served on its faculty (~1979–2014), teaching Ilkka Pyysiäinen.

René Grousset (1885–1952), a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology, studied at the University of Montpellier (~1903–1906). He held posts at the Guimet Museum, Musée Cernuschi, École du Louvre, and Louvre Museum.

René Guénon (1886–1951) was a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. His education included studies at the Robert-Badinter School Complex (1902–1903), Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour (1904–1906), and the University of Paris (1914–1917).

René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz (1923–1959) worked in Tibetology and religious studies. Educated at Vienna, SOAS, Berlin, and LSE, he studied under Wilhelm Koppers, Giuseppe Tucci, and others. In 1958, he was a wissenschaftlicher Beamter at the Weltmuseum Wien.
Rewa Prasad Dwivedi (1935–2021) was an Indology scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University. He also served there as Head of Sahityavidya from circa 1977 to 1995.

Rewata Dhamma (1929–2004) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned his BA, MA, and PhD at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University between 1956 and 1967, and completed a doctorate at Banaras Hindu University (1956–1967).

Richard A. Hutch (born 1945) is a religious studies scholar who studied at Gettysburg College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He held faculty posts at Southern Illinois University (~1974–1978) and the University of Queensland (~1978–2010).

Richard B. Mahoney works in Buddhist and computational studies. He completed an MA at the University of Canterbury by 2002 under the supervision of Paul Harrison, having held a post at the same university in 2001.
Richard B. Martin is an Indology and Tibetology scholar. At the University of Virginia, he served as a professor (attested 1983–1991) and later as a South Asian bibliographer (attested 2003).

Richard Baker (born 1936) is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Harvard and UC Berkeley, and trained under Shunryu Suzuki. He founded the San Francisco Zen Center (1962), serving as its abbot from 1971 to 1984, and founded Dharma Sangha.
Richard Barron is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge.

Richard Bowring (born 1947), a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies, earned his BA, doctorate, and Litt.D at Cambridge. He taught at Columbia, Princeton, and Cambridge (where he was later Emeritus Professor), and served as Master of Selwyn College (2000–2012).

Richard Carnac Temple (1850–1931) studied at Harrow and Trinity Hall, Cambridge. Working in Indology and archaeology, he edited *Indian Antiquary* (~1884–1910), founded *Panjab Notes and Queries* (1883), and served in the Bengal and Indian Staff Corps.
Richard D. Mann is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his PhD at McMaster University under Phyllis Granoff (attested 2003). He held a post at Carleton University (attested 2007).

Richard D. McBride II is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD at UCLA under mentor Robert E. Buswell Jr. He held positions at Dongguk University and Brigham Young University, alongside a fellowship at Washington University.

Richard Delbrueck (1875–1957) was an archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Bonn (~1895–1899). He held academic posts at Bonn (~1908–1911), the University of Jena (~1922–1928), and the University of Giessen (~1928–1940).

Richard F. Nance is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of Chicago in 2004. He has held assistant and associate professor posts in religious studies at Indiana University Bloomington.
